sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Wolverhampton host Sunderland at Molineux with the hosts bottom (20th, 17 points) and the visitors mid-table (12th, 46 points). Sofascore’s model gives a slight away edge (home 31%, draw 31%, away 38%) and a low chance of both teams scoring (38%).

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Wolverhampton are winless in 5 (0-1-4) and have not scored in their last 3. Sunderland have won 2 of their last 5 but come in off heavy defeats to Aston Villa and Nottingham Forest after a solid run that included wins over Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Sunderland won the reverse fixture 2-0 and are unbeaten in the last meetings, keeping clean sheets throughout (team streaks note 4 without conceding). Recent head-to-head results have tilted towards Sunderland’s control without giving up many chances.

sections.subtitle: Season stats snapshot
sections.text: Wolverhampton have the league’s fewest goals (24, rank 20) and fewest big chances created (42, rank 20), with only 4 clean sheets (rank 19) and 62 conceded (rank 19). Sunderland sit 12th (36 scored, 45 conceded), profiling as a balanced mid-table side.

sections.subtitle: Tactical notes and key players
sections.text: Wolverhampton rely on crosses (high accuracy rank) but struggle for sustained final-third presence and penalty-area entries. Sunderland’s threat is spread: Brian Brobbey leads their scoring, Enzo Le Fée creates, and Nordi Mukiele impressed in the reverse fixture; Granit Xhaka has been effective against this opponent.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Referee Paul Tierney averages 3.2 yellows and 0.12 reds. Wolverhampton commit many fouls and average 2.15 yellows per match; away matches trend under on corners for Sunderland (less than 10.5 in 4/5). Expect a moderate card count and a relatively low corner total.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Model probabilities point to Sunderland edging a tight contest, with both teams to score less likely. Given Wolverhampton’s recent goal drought and Sunderland’s clean-sheet trend in this matchup, the visitors are favoured to take the points in a low-margin game.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context and half-time summary
halftimeSections.text: Sunderland lead 1-0 at Molineux after Nordi Mukiele’s 17’ header, with Granit Xhaka providing the decisive delivery. The match turned when Daniel Ballard was sent off, leaving Sunderland with 10. Wolves responded with sustained pressure before the interval and created the better chances late in the half.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key stats at the break
halftimeSections.text: Expected goals: Wolves 0.60, Sunderland 0.33. Shots on target: 2-2. Corners: 4-2 to Wolves. Possession: 51-49 to Wolves. Penalty area entries: 17-12 to Wolves. Big chances: Wolves 1 (missed), Sunderland 1 (scored). Aerial duels won: Wolves 56%.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Sunderland enjoyed a strong spell around the goal, building sustained pressure through the middle of the half. After the dismissal, Wolves took control, with an extended attacking spell from the mid-30s to the break and repeated waves just before half-time.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical outlook for the second half
halftimeSections.text: With a man advantage, Wolves should raise their full-backs and attack wide through Hugo Bueno and Pedro Lima, delivering early crosses towards Tolu Arokodare and targeting second balls for Mateus Mané and João Gomes. Set pieces look valuable given Wolves’ edge in the air. Sunderland are likely to drop into a compact 4-4-1, with Xhaka screening and playing long diagonals for Brian Brobbey and Chemsdine Talbi to chase. Transitions remain their best route, but they will need to manage crosses and avoid isolating the centre-backs.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: First half cards: Sunderland 1 yellow, 1 red; Wolves 0. With Sunderland defending deep, expect further cautions for the away side. Corners stood at 4-2 to Wolves at the break; with continued home pressure, expect Wolves to add 3-4 more after the restart, with Sunderland limited to 1-2.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Given the red card and late first-half pressure, Wolves are well placed to turn territory into goals. Expect the next goal to come from Wolves, with Arokodare the most likely scorer from a cross or set piece. Sunderland can threaten on the break, but sustained defending should tell. Predicted final score: Wolves 2-1 Sunderland.
